points: The Nov 6 Q3 print will reveal whether the CARFAX go-to-market recalibration is stabilizing revenue or still dragging growth, which is the key driver of any FY1/FY2 estimate revision.

Reports suggest full-year 2026 revenue guidance is $1.870B-$1.885B; Q3 revenue performance and any update to that range will show if the top-line trajectory can support the ~4.99% FY2 EPS growth baked into consensus.
Q2 2026 reportedly saw revenue rise but earnings fall; the Q3 print must clarify whether that margin pressure was temporary or the start of sustained compression.
With the stock at roughly 12.97x FY1 earnings and 6.47x sales, fair versus the theme, the print needs to create estimate momentum rather than rely on a valuation rerating.

Peer prints from CNXC, EXLS, and VRRM in late October/early November will set the demand/pricing backdrop; weak read-throughs would make it harder for MBGL to produce the +0.5% revision needed for a long.

The decisive outcome is the direction of FY1/FY2 EPS revisions after the print: guidance or results that push consensus up more than 0.5% would create a long, while a cut or soft outlook that pushes it down more than 0.5% would create a short.
watch: Q3 revenue vs the $1.870B-$1.885B full-year 2026 guide and any range change: maintaining or raising supports a long, lowering kills the long and supports a shor
Gross/operating margin trend after Q2 earnings fell: expansion or stability supports a long, further compression supports a short.
FY1/FY2 EPS revision direction post-print: above +0.5% establishes a long, below -0.5% establishes a short.
CARFAX recalibration commentary: evidence of stabilization supports a long, continued disruption supports a short.
